title: Nonlinear creatine kinase does not improve frozen handgrip prediction over conventional covariates and linear logCK
abstract: We tested a sex-specific nonlinear serum creatine kinase (CK) response as an additional representation of muscle-state information in public physiological data. Models fit in NHANES2011–2012 (n=3916) were frozen and evaluated in separately recruited2013–2014 (n=4412). The comparator used flexible anthropometry, serum creatinine/albumin, demographics and sex-specific linear logCK. Replacing the latter with cubic logCK splines increased target weighted mean squared error from 127.5497 to 132.0234 kg²; delta +4.4737, joint source/target rescaled-PSU bootstrap95% interval [-0.3923,+19.3829]. The improvement criterion was not met. Tail influence and spline complexity affected the size of harm, while all tested sensitivity point estimates remained nonbeneficial. This exploratory negative result concerns this prediction task and specification, not absence of biological CK information or clinical utility in other settings.
